source.title: FTA Corporate Tax Guide CTGBRR1, April 2024

findings: Official guidance establishes that restructuring relief is a conditional regime; an absence record would not close these slots correctly.
Guidance is not legally binding; authoritative legislation and later amendments must be verified before admitting executable rules.
Eligibility, election, carryover basis and subsequent clawback require distinct facts, not a blanket zero rate.

coverage_interpretation: The 30 gaps are planner jurisdiction/subject/slot cells. They are not a count of failed income-assessment tests or proof of statutory absence.

ministerial_decision.important_branch: Article 8(2) allocates clawback gain/loss to the transferee if the transferor is a natural person or has ceased to be taxable.

current_law_verification.limitation: Listing exposes 10 of 52 entries; this is not proof that MD 133 has no later amendment. Publication date must be established independently of issue date.

consolidated_law_lead.note: MOF January 2026 consolidated English publication; Arabic prevails. Search excerpt explicitly references FDL 28/2025. Later amendments still require verification.

article27_comparison.normalization: Whitespace and standalone page numbers removed; wording retained
article27_comparison.limitation: A match verifies this article between these two publications, not absence of all later amendments.
article27_comparison.difference_review: Token diff contains list-label punctuation changes (a) to a. etc.) and removal of repeating historical translation footer only; no substantive Article 27 wording difference observed.

implementation_boundary.current_transaction: Planner via/direct operations transfer shares in a target, not necessarily a whole business or independent business unit.
implementation_boundary.required_distinction: Article 27 relief cannot automatically apply to an ordinary share disposal. A business-transfer qualification must be explicit.
